title: The Thalidomide Children
text: The Thalidomide Tragedy Warning: Topic includes Medical Gore and Incompetence. We take paracetamol, tylenol, or any other OTC drugs for pain, headaches, what not.. We feel a sense of security with these drugs as they have gone through extensive clinical trials and testing, and the process (for the most part), remains quite bulletproof and trustworthy to the average consumer. What happens, when this system of quality control for our medication, is not reliable AT ALL?! Normally, clinical trials in modern medicine proceeds through several (or a combination of) regulated stages: preclinical laboratory and animal testing, followed by Phase I safety testing, Phase II efficacy and dosing studies, and large Phase III controlled trials. Only after sufficient evidence of safety and effectiveness is reviewed by regulators can a drug be approved, with Phase IV monitoring continuing after release. Rewind to shortly after WW2 Thalidomide was first developed as a tranquilizer by Swiss pharmaceutical company Ciba in 1953. The drug was abandoned in 1954 and was acquired by German pharmaceutical company Chemie Grünenthal. (Yes the company was established by a Nazi, but that's not the point of this topic.) Grünenthal administered thalidomide to laboratory animals and found remarkably low acute toxicity. Researchers reportedly had difficulty establishing an LD50 (the dose that kills half the test animals), which contributed to the belief that it was much safer than barbiturate sleeping drugs. Thalidomide was released in Germany in 1957 and subsequently distributed internationally under numerous trade names. Yeah.. That's the extent to the testing of this drugs. On Animals. Early human testing focused largely on its sedative effects and immediate toxicity, so a lot went under the hood during its release. The big overlook, was the drugs' affect on embryonic development in pregnant women. But even before the birth-defect connection became established, reports emerged of peripheral neuropathy in adults taking thalidomide for prolonged periods. Just making this point to show how avoidable this scandal could have been. Now coming to the Elephant, the Thalidomide Children. Reports emerged of children born with severely malformed or absent limbs, alongside abnormalities affecting the ears, eyes and internal organs. At first, these cases baffled physicians, who observed the sudden rise in rare congenital defects but did not know what was causing them. In 1961, the connection became clear independently to German physician Widukind Lenz and Australian obstetrician William McBride, who noticed that many affected pregnancies shared one thing, the mothers had taken thalidomide.

title: An Ode to Kentaro Miura's Berserk
text: My favourite piece of art of all time, and I feel blessed and grateful to have a genius like Kentaro Miura present a part of his soul to us. I don't want to talk about Berserk, read it yourself, if you haven't already. I have instead, written my own short non-canon story that takes place in the Berserk Universe, and runs independent to the plot of Berserk. Rest in Peace Miura. Emperor Ganishka Daiba Warning: Topics include War, War Crimes, Psychopathy and PTSD. "The Kushan dynasty never saw a reason to get involved with The Midland and Tudor war, we faced troubles with some skirmishes within our ranks, as is usual, but firmly sit on all the wealth of the Sikkimese, Mauryas, and the Cholas." a brief silence enters the room, as the King's councilmember continues "Still, It's in Kushan's best interest if Midland lose the war, we are close neighbours, and rumor has it that the Midland Army have an ace up their sleeve, a white hawk. " King Ganishka, the ever ambitious Emperor of Kushan listened not to the bickering of his Councilmen, because he had already been planning a Midland Invasion for the past 6 months. You can't be too careful in the den of viper called The Royal Palace, but only a handful of Ganishka's most loyal servants knew of the plot. His most loyal of them was Daiba. He met a sorcerer during his Sikkim conquest named Daiba. He could fly and manipulate water and wind, and was well versed in the Occult. During his Sikkim expedition, Ganishka came across an odd rock, Crimson red and what looked like features of a visage, a shallow beat could be felt within the rock, it was obvious this rock was of the occult. Shortly after encountering the rock, Ganishka comes across Daiba, who joined his ranks 2 days later as his Court Sorcerer. Daiba Examines the rock and proclaims it as "The Egg of the King", a fated rock that reveals itself only under pure suffering. "A king's trophy, for the egg contains a lake of blood, and in blood only will the egg hatch." Daiba's Prophesy taps into Ganishka's clear bloodlust. The Councilmen did not trust Daiba, for he felt like an outsider whispering dark crude sorcery to the kings ears, only titillating the sanguinarian king further. But Kushan wouldn't go to war for the next two years. The Sikkim expedition was an expensive endeavor. Kushan lost 1/5th of its infantry, and The Kingdom was fatigued. Despite this Kushan still had over 350,000 troops, along with the artillery, mobilized spanning to the borders of Paneria. (For reference, at the apex of the 100 year war, Tudor had 150,000 mobilized men and Midland were 80,000 small. ) But, timing of the war made no sense for kushan to get involved. Midland might be small, but they've been stubborn on the battlefield, and whispers of the hawks reputation and excellence on the battlefield reached the King's ears more than a few times. "We'll clean up the mess when the time comes" Emperor Ganishka, as he dismisses his court. "Daiba, not you." The Garrisons turn. The Crown Prince draws his sword, with the implicit order, the garrisons and councilmen followed their new leader. Ganishka, filled with the ecstasy of his own blood loss, he looked into his son's eyes. It was like a mirror was put in front of him, the same paranoia, regicidal, A circle of usurpation. title: Asano Inio's Oyasumi Punpun
text: Punpun and Aiko as Children "God" Midori and Yuichi Punpun and Aiko as adults Transformation of Punpun Sachi The Tragedy of Aiko Oyasumi Punpun Warning: Topic Includes Suicide, Violence, Loss of Innocence, Tragedy and Rape. this manga broke me Things I'm going to ignore: The Pegasus cult sideplot, although quite a nice metaphor for the main story, its not important. The full extent of Punpun's visual transformation. I will cover it a bit, because Inio did an amazing job here, but I don't feel I can do justice to it. ... Punpun Onodera is an ordinary elementary-school kid. He smiles, laughs, likes to play and look at the stars, like a regular kid. Punpun's home is dysfunctional. His father is violent, his mother is emotionally unstable and neglectful. One day, Punpun's father violently assaults his mother, leaving her seriously injured and hospitalized. Following her Hospitalization, he abandons the family. Punpun finds solace in stars, space, and his school crush Aiko. Actually, he also has an eccentric uncle, Yuichi Onodera, and his imaginary friend "God", but I will come back to them later. Punpun is head over heels for Aiko. Aiko herself, is strange, intense and unhappy. Her mother belongs to a cultish religious organization, and Aiko desperately wants to escape her home. She tells Punpun about Kagoshima, where she once lived, and the two make a childish promise that they'll go there together. Punpun hypes himself up to do it, escaping his life to go with the love of his life. He psyches himself out to the point where he feels an overwhelming sense of urgency and responsibility of it, and he ends up not going with Aiko. Punpun is naturally a bit of a wimp. "God" Yuichi and Midori Punpun's transformations Sachi Aiko's suicide The light at the end of the tunnel...

title: Lilja-4-Ever (2002)
text: Lilja-4-Ever (2002) Warning: T opic includ es Child Exploitation, Rape , Human Trafficking and Suicide. Sometimes similar art are cited as being depraved and tragic for the sake of it, either horror sensationalism or some flavorless psychopath porn. Lilja-4-Ever is not one of these, despite being one of the most uncomfortable films of all time. Lilja-4-ever was a difficult watch, and is an extremely depressing movie to ruminate over. Obligatory information: This Swedish movie takes place in some former Soviet country and is Russian(language) for the most part. Released in 2002 and directed by Lukas Moodysson, the movie follows 16yo girl, Lilja after her mother abandons her, leaving her to survive alone amid poverty in a deeply cynical dump of a corner in some post-soviet bloc. This movie is based on, and is incredibly faithful to the real tragedy of Danguolė Rasalaitė , A lithuanian girl who came to Sweden in 1999, with the belief she would work as a berry picker, forced into prostitution, and took her own life at the age of 16. There are 3 things I wish to discuss regarding this film: Lilja I like the word apathy here, because it reflects not just on the entire environment, but especially on Lilja herself. Lilja, is a teenager by all accounts. She's rude, abrasive, obnoxious, combative the most time, as is a teenagers' nature. She grew up with a mother until the age of 16, which appears to be a privilege in and of itself in the poverty stricken areas of the bloc. Her mother marries a man who is moving to the states, promising to bring Lilja with her, but couldn't (you think money grows on trees bro?). She eventually sends Lilja a letter saying she abandons her. (I will talk about this more a bit later) She was frequently harassed, belittled, and was a bit of a trash can for her neighbors and "friends". This is an abandoned teenage girl that has nothing going her way, she has nothing to be thankful about, especially since her Aunt claimed the apartment (has a heater) left by Lilja's mother. "Go to an orphanage, Go to a friend house, or Go spread your legs out on the street like your mother did." -Lilja's Aunt The one silver lining in her life was Volodya, a scrawny 14 yo boy who loved playing basketball. Their relationship is extremely wholesome. For instance, Lilja eventually, in order to literally eat, voluntarily prostitutes herself, and takes care of Volodya, and buys him a new Basketball too. Volodya has an Alcoholic father who beats him, so Volodya stays away from home as much as possible. Volodya and Lilja form a bond that become a safe haven for both of them. One night amidst a party, Lilja comes across a charming guy in his early 20s, Human Trafficking I will not insult the victims of trafficking by politicizing it, because its purely predatory. Lilja did have a friend her age, The De-stalinization of the Soviet Union This conversation between Lilja and Volodya in the movie hit me deep, as they stare at a mural of the Red Star. “Something happened here 50 years ago, and thats why everything sucks”. -Lilja to Volodya Lithuania was one of the Soviet Puppet states that was a victim of Soviet Communism. Without going into too much detail (refer to my retrospective of Come and See (1985)), the eastern bloc got really screwed for multiple decades. In 1985, after Mikhail Gorbachev loosening of the Soviet Blocs, Lithuania gained their Independence through some good old fashion revolution-ing. But the poor still suffered much after the Independence, and the apathetic and destitute environment we see in Lilja show aspects of Eastern Europe that are still recovering from Stalin and Communism. The Iron Curtain may have fallen, but Eastern Europe still bled for a while. It is important we know the history, but, I appreciate this movie for not being antagonistic to anything political. "Something happened, but we have our world in front of us, and I don't need any history to know how much Humanity sucks." I like to think this is what Lilja meant. But let this film, and by extention, the life of Rasalaitė, be recognized as the consequences of the poor political decisions made by the Soviet Union between 1930-1983.
